project_type: .NET 8 WPF desktop app (WorshipPlayer) — Core class library + net8.0-windows WPF Presenter, assembled by WorshipPlayer.UI; xUnit test project.
build_system: dotnet SDK (MSBuild). Solution has WorshipPlayer.Core (net8.0), WorshipPlayer.Presenter (net8.0-windows WPF), WorshipPlayer.Audio, WorshipPlayer.UI (startup), WorshipPlayer.Tests (net8.0).
test_framework: xUnit (WorshipPlayer.Tests). It references WorshipPlayer.Core by ProjectReference and LINKS individual Presenter sources via <Compile Include> (it cannot reference the WPF Presenter assembly, which is net8.0-windows). So any logic that must be unit-tested must live in Core, not in the WPF code-behind.
build_command: dotnet build WorshipPlayer.UI/WorshipPlayer.UI.csproj -c Debug  (run from the worktree root)
test_command: dotnet test  (filter new tests: dotnet test --filter "FullyQualifiedName~SlideServiceItemEditorModelTests")
verification_instructions: From the worktree root run `dotnet build WorshipPlayer.UI/WorshipPlayer.UI.csproj -c Debug` then `dotnet test`. NEVER run clean or delete bin/obj — runtime data (app.db, service JSONs) lives under bin. Use `git -C <worktree>` for git.
environment_constraints: Windows. All work targets the worktree c:\Users\Quang\Documents\OneWorshipcenter\owc-multitrack-feature-lyric-presenter\owc-multitrack-feature-lyric-presenter\.worktrees\slide-item-editor on branch feature/slide-item-editor — NOT the repo root. Every file path must be absolute under the worktree; relative paths risk landing in the parent workspace. NEVER clean/delete bin/obj. SQLite is accessed only via the shared AppDatabase (Microsoft.Data.Sqlite), no EF. SQLite connection pools keep a file handle open on Windows — temp-db tests must call SqliteConnection.ClearAllPools() in teardown before deleting the temp folder (see TemplateServiceTests).
contribution_requirements: No AGENTS.md/CONTRIBUTING/.kiro steering files exist in the repo. Follow the APPROVED design.md and requirements.md under .agents/tasks/slide-item-editor. Model changes are ADDITIVE and backward-compatible only; the three real service-order JSON files and demo files must still load. Additive nullable fields are omitted from JSON when null (WhenWritingNull convention). Commit locally on the branch; never push.
key_patterns: Peer editors are owned modal Windows opened with ShowDialog (SlideEditorWindow, ItemSettingsWindow, AddServiceItemDialog). A standalone Window merges pack://application:,,,/WorshipPlayer.Presenter;component/Themes/OwcDesignSystem.xaml in Window.Resources and uses KEYED StaticResource styles (OwcButtonBase, OwcBlueButton, OwcTextBox, OwcPanelBorder, OwcTextSecondaryBrush, OwcDarkComboBox, OwcSlider). OperatorWindow.xaml itself declares NO ResourceDictionary and uses inline hex brushes — but this editor is a separate Window, so it uses keyed styles like SlideEditorWindow (do NOT copy OperatorWindow's inline-brush rule). Display name resolves live via ServiceItemDisplayName.ResolveDisplayName(item, linked) — a PURE two-arg helper, no cache/service access, no one-arg overload. Auto-advance label<->enum mapping lives in ItemSettingsMapping (next to ItemSettingsPanel) and delegates the after-condition to BulkEditService.ParseAfterCondition so bulk and per-item edit agree. Persistence: ServiceOrderManager.SaveAsync writes authoritative JSON then best-effort upserts the ServiceOrders.DataJson SQLite mirror with the same _jsonOptions (WriteIndented + WhenWritingNull + JsonStringEnumConverter); additive fields flow into both automatically — no manager/schema change.
